learningObjectives: Create and inspect references in the Execution tab.
Distinguish latest summaries, per-entry history and archived snapshots.
Run selected execution objects with F6 and inspect result context.

elements.text: ExecutionLists organize TestCase references in the Execution tab. Drag a TestCase onto an existing list to create an ExecutionEntry; dragging a TestCase folder can create a linked entry folder. The structure can contain further folders, rather than exactly three universal levels.

By default, the same TestCase can be dragged onto the same list only once. Repetitions can repeat an entry with the same values. For multiple references with differing values, configure MultipleReferencesToIdenticalTestCaseAllowed and the entry TCPs deliberately.

ActualLog summarizes the latest run and is overwritten on rerun. Each executed entry gets a new TestCaseLog; ArchivedLog captures a snapshot when created. This is recorded history, not a guarantee of undeletable permanent retention. ScratchBook trials are temporary.

Passed, Failed, Error and No result are distinct. An environment/test problem can produce Error; missing results do not prove a preceding test blocked execution. The documented Skipped result is specific to SeaLights integration. Inspect the actual log detail.

elements.caption: Independent list/result example: configure repetitions and inspect logs rather than assuming unlimited default insertion.

elements.text: Create a folder and an empty ExecutionList in the Execution tab, then drop the intended TestCases directly on the list. Inspect the created references, effective parameter values and prepared SUT state. Independent team readiness checks may include completion/review; WorkState is not a universal creation prerequisite.

Run selected execution objects through the context menu or F6. Rearrange entries to change order; disabled entries are omitted. Run from here starts at the chosen entry. Execution behavior and dependencies must be configured rather than assumed from a prior failure.

Independent inspection exercise: run a disposable case twice and compare latest summary versus per-entry logs. Prepare and review the SUT prerequisites. Original Academy Exercise 21 was inaccessible and was not executed.
Academy Exercise 21 requires authorized course access. Its original procedure, figures and success state were not verified; the local practice is independent documentation-based guidance.

examPitfalls.title: Default vs repetition
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure repetitions or multiple references appropriately.

examPitfalls.title: Summary vs history
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect per-entry logs and archived snapshots.

examPitfalls.title: Result context
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating No result as proof of a preceding failure.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect whether and how the entry ran.

examPitfalls.title: Readiness
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating COMPLETED as a universal insertion requirement.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Apply deliberate team readiness and data checks.

examPitfalls.title: F6 context
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming F6 can only run ScratchBook.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Selected execution objects can also run with F6.

practiceQuiz.scenario: With default settings, how often can the same TestCase be dragged onto the same ExecutionList before configuring multiple references?

options.text: Once by default; repetitions and multiple-reference configuration are separate options.
Repeated execution is impossible under any configuration.
Twice — a maximum of two entries per TestCase per ExecutionList.
The limit is set in the TestCase properties tab.

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish default insertion from configured repetition.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Default drag/drop allows one reference; repetition or configured multiple references can provide additional execution.

optionExplanations.A: This separates the default from supported repeat mechanisms.
optionExplanations.C: There is no documented default two-entry allowance.
optionExplanations.D: This is not the documented configuration location.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to quickly run a single TestCase without setting up a formal ExecutionList. What built-in feature of Tosca Commander should they use?

options.text: The Debug Console.
The ScratchBook.
The TestCase Viewer.
A temporary ExecutionList that auto-deletes after execution.

practiceQuiz.hint: It is a pre-existing, built-in ad-hoc execution area.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ScratchBook provides trial runs without retained list/history setup; prepare the SUT prerequisites.

optionExplanations.A: This is not the documented trial area.
optionExplanations.C: Viewing alone is not this trial capability.
optionExplanations.D: No automatic self-deleting list is required.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In which section of Tosca Commander are ExecutionLists found?

options.text: In the TestCases section, as a sub-folder of the test hierarchy.
In the Modules section, alongside module definitions.
In the Execution tab, separate from TestCases and Modules.
In the Requirements section, linked to requirement coverage.

practiceQuiz.hint: Each major area in Tosca has its own section.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Execution organization is separate from models and TestCase definitions; Commander has other sections too.

optionExplanations.A: Definitions are separate from execution organization.
optionExplanations.C: This is the documented execution area.
optionExplanations.D: Coverage links do not move lists into Requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which feature supports retained per-entry execution logs across runs, rather than only temporary trial results?

options.text: The ScratchBook — it archives every run automatically.
The Modules section.
The TestCase WorkState field.
An ExecutionList with TestCaseLogs; ActualLog is only the latest summary.

practiceQuiz.hint: A latest summary and history are different objects.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Entry logs record runs; ActualLog alone is overwritten. Retention still depends on log management.

optionExplanations.A: Trial runs do not archive each run.
optionExplanations.B: Technical models do not hold this run history.
optionExplanations.C: Progress state is not execution history.
optionExplanations.D: Entry logs record runs; the summary is latest-only.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants three TestCases represented as entries in one already-created ExecutionList. What is the appropriate drag/drop target?

options.text: Drop the TestCases directly onto the existing ExecutionList and inspect the created entries.
Change WorkState to force every folder into one list.
A single list can never contain multiple TestCases.
Changing Business Parameter values creates execution entries automatically.

practiceQuiz.rationale: The existing list is the direct target for adding its entries.

optionExplanations.A: This adds entries to the intended list.
optionExplanations.B: Progress state does not select this target.
optionExplanations.C: A list can organize several cases.
optionExplanations.D: Reference data values do not create entries by themselves.
